area_overview: Core time representation and transport/display basics for ASP.NET/Core and JS frontends.
key_ideas: Use DateTimeOffset for API/database timestamps and store/compare instants in UTC.
Plain DateTime depends on Kind and is ambiguous when Kind is Unspecified.
DateOnly, TimeOnly, and TimeSpan represent non-instant domain values and durations.
DateTimeOffset offset means UTC = local clock time - offset.
Ticks are .NET-specific 100 ns units since year 0001; Unix time is seconds/milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC.
For frontend interop, ISO strings are readable and Unix milliseconds are convenient for JS Date/arithmetic/timers.
JS locale formatting methods are display-only and should match the user's locale/timezone.
